answer:
**Tokenization can make equivalent messages consume different amounts of context.** A vocabulary well matched to English may encode common words compactly while splitting an Indic-script or Romanized phrase into many pieces. Measure the actual tokenizer and corpus; a universal three-to-five-times factor is not justified. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06226)

If one text requires k times as many tokens, KV storage for that text grows roughly by k. Dense attention's score interactions can grow by k squared during processing of the longer sequence. Token-based billing can also increase, but full latency depends on projections, kernels, batching, and decoding.

**Compression and quality are separate.** A larger multilingual vocabulary can shorten sequences but increases embedding/output tables and may include poorly trained rare entries. Romanized spelling variation can remain difficult even with many vocabulary entries.

Compare tokens per byte or character alongside meaningful task quality across languages, scripts, and domains. Preserve normalization conventions and rare names in the evaluation. The relevant question is whether users receive comparable useful capacity and latency, not merely whether the vocabulary contains some tokens from their language.

**Technical details and references.**

An English-heavy vocabulary may encode common English words compactly while splitting Indic scripts or Romanized variants into many smaller pieces. This increases tokens per semantic unit, but the prompt's 3–5× factor must be measured for the tokenizer and corpus. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06226)

If input length grows by $k$, token-based billing may grow roughly $k$ for that portion, dense attention score work by $k^2$, and KV memory by $k$. Whole-request latency does not necessarily scale quadratically because projections, kernels, batching, and decode differ.

Measure fertility by language, bytes, script, and domain; compare quality as well as compression. Larger multilingual vocabularies trade sequence length against embedding/output size and training coverage for rare tokens.
